lines.text: What violent physics occurs in the first sixty seconds when a giant orbital rocket lifts off?
At liftoff, giant rocket engines consume thousands of gallons of liquid propellant every second.
Giant water deluge trenches dump four hundred thousand gallons of water to dampen acoustic shockwaves.
By second thirty, the rocket pushes past the speed of sound, creating a visible condensation shock cone.
At second sixty, the rocket hits Max Q, the point of maximum aerodynamic stress on the vehicle's frame.
Rushing through thick atmosphere at two thousand miles per hour, engines throttle down to prevent ripping apart.
Surviving those first sixty seconds is the hardest physical hurdle of reaching outer space.
